name: Pink
description:
'''Alecia Beth Moore-Hart''' (born September 8, 1979), known professionally as '''Pink''' (stylized as {{nowrap|'''P!nk'''}}), is an American singer and songwriter. She is known for her powerful vocal range and acrobatic stage presence.

After signing with [[LaFace Records]] in 1995, Pink began her career as part of the girl group Choice, although they disbanded without any major releases. As a solo artist, she released her [[contemporary R&B|R&B]]-influenced debut studio album, ''[[Can't Take Me Home]]'' (2000), before achieving wider recognition with her [[pop rock]] albums ''[[Missundaztood]]'' (2001), ''[[Try This]]'' (2003), ''[[I'm Not Dead]]'' (2006), and ''[[Funhouse (Pink album)|Funhouse]]'' (2008). She topped the US [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]] with her next albums ''[[The Truth About Love]]'' (2012), ''[[Beautiful Trauma]]'' (2017) and ''[[Hurts 2B Human]]'' (2019). Her ninth studio album, ''[[Trustfall]]'' (2023), was promoted with the [[Summer Carnival (tour)|Summer Carnival]] tour, which became the [[List of highest-grossing concert tours by women|second-highest grossing concert tour by a woman]]. Pink's catalog of high-charting singles include: "[[There You Go]]", "[[Most Girls (Pink song)|Most Girls]]", "[[Lady Marmalade#Moulin Rouge! version|Lady Marmalade]]", "[[Get the Party Started]]", "[[Don't Let Me Get Me]]", "[[Just Like a Pill]]", "[[Who Knew]]", "[[U + Ur Hand]]", "[[So What (Pink song)|So What]]", "[[Raise Your Glass]]", and "[[Just Give Me a Reason]]".

Pink has sold more than 135 million records worldwide, making her one of the [[List of best-selling music artists|world's best-selling music artists]]. Pink is the most-played female solo artist in the UK during the 21st century, while [[Billboard (magazine)|''Billboard'']] named Pink the [[Pop Airplay|Pop Songs]] [[Billboard Decade-End#2000s|Artist of the 2000s Decade]]. [[List of awards and nominations received by Pink|Her accolades]] include three [[Grammy Awards]], two [[Brit Awards]], a [[Daytime Emmy Award]], seven [[MTV Video Music Awards]], and two [[MTV Europe Music Awards]]. At the 63rd [[BMI Award|BMI Pop Awards]], she received the BMI President's Award for "her outstanding achievement in songwriting and global impact on pop culture and the entertainment industry", and was honored with the [[People's Choice Awards|People's Champion Award]], the [[IHeartRadio Music Awards|iHeartRadio Music Award Icon Award]]. ''Billboard'' named Pink the 2013 Woman of the Year at the [[Billboard Women in Music|''Billboard'' Women in Music]] and honored her with the [[Billboard Icon Award|''Billboard'' Icon Award]] and the [[Billboard Live Music Awards|''Billboard'' Legend of Live]]. [[VH1]] ranked her 10th on its list of the [[The Greatest (VH1 TV series)|100 Greatest Women in Music]]. In 2026, Pink was nominated for the [[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]].
